title: Quickstart templates — CI & Release Plan (draft)
content:
Context
- This doc defines the draft CI and release process for the Quickstart templates initiative (RAG, agents, combined RAG+agent) in redwood-quickstarts, plus the supporting observability pack.
- Goals:
  - Make template releases predictable and boring.
  - Keep “time-to-first-success” high by preventing drift between docs/snippets and actual repos.
  - Catch common support drivers before they ship (429 handling, streaming disconnects behind proxies, missing timeouts/retries, telemetry not emitted, env var mismatches).
  - Ensure template contract changes are versioned and communicated.
- Non-goal: reinvent a full release engineering framework. Keep this lightweight and automatable.

Repo layout (assumption)
- redwood-quickstarts (monorepo)
  - templates/python-rag-fastapi
  - templates/ts-rag
  - templates/agents
  - templates/rag-agent
  - packages/shared-config (env/config loader)
  - packages/shared-telemetry (OTel + log correlation)
  - docs/ (template READMEs, production checklist, env var reference)
- observability-pack
  - dashboards/
  - alerts/
  - import/README

Versioning strategy
1) What we version
- Template bundle (redwood-quickstarts): versioned as a single unit to avoid matrix explosion.
- Observability pack: versioned separately but aligned with telemetry contract versions.
- Telemetry contract: treated as an interface; changes require explicit version bump and migration notes.

2) Version scheme
- Use SemVer for redwood-quickstarts releases: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
  - PATCH: bug fixes, doc fixes, dependency bumps that don’t change behavior in a user-visible way (or only make defaults safer), improvements that don’t break template contract.
  - MINOR: additive features (new template, new optional backend, new metrics), default changes that could affect behavior but are backwards compatible at the contract level.
  - MAJOR: breaking changes to env vars, folder structure, request/response shapes in template APIs, removal of a supported backend, telemetry contract break (e.g., rename required metric), or any change that invalidates previous setup instructions.

3) Compatibility matrix
- Each redwood-quickstarts release must publish/refresh a compatibility matrix:
  - Minimum supported redwood SDK versions (Python + TypeScript)
  - Supported Node/Python versions
  - Supported vector DB backend(s) and their versions (for default docker-compose path)
  - Telemetry contract version
- Where it lives:
  - /docs/COMPATIBILITY.md (human-friendly)
  - /docs/COMPATIBILITY.csv (easy copy into docs site)
- Policy:
  - Support the latest 2 minor template releases (N and N-1) for patch fixes.
  - When a new minor is released, N-2 becomes security-fixes-only for 30 days, then EOL.

4) Tags + releases
- All releases are tagged in Git:
  - redwood-quickstarts: vX.Y.Z
  - observability-pack: vX.Y.Z
- Release notes:
  - Auto-generated from PR labels (feature/fix/breaking/docs/chore/security)
  - Must include:
    - Any template contract changes (env vars, endpoints)
    - Telemetry changes (new required fields, renamed metrics)
    - Upgrade notes for users (copy/paste commands)

Branching + change management
- Main branch is always releasable.
- Use short-lived feature branches; avoid long-running release branches.
- PR requirements for merge:
  - CI green (see CI matrix)
  - Review from:
    - DX owner for template code
    - SRE for operational defaults if timeouts/retry/circuit-breaker changes
    - Security reviewer for secrets/logging/tool calling changes
    - Telemetry platform reviewer if metrics/log fields/trace attrs change

Release cadence
- Default cadence: biweekly MINOR releases during launch window (Jan–Mar), then monthly.
- PATCH releases as needed (esp. response to support tickets) with expedited path.
- MAJOR releases: only with explicit launch plan + deprecation window.

CI overview
- CI is split into:
  1) Fast checks (PR gating): <10 minutes target
  2) Full matrix checks (merge gating): may be longer, runs on merge queue and nightly
  3) E2E smoke tests against staging: runs on merge (or scheduled) + on release candidates

CI matrix (draft)
A) Lint + formatting
- Python: ruff + black (or ruff format) + mypy for typed modules
- TypeScript: eslint + prettier + tsc
- YAML/JSON: schema validation for dashboards/alerts if applicable
- Markdown: lint for code block validity + link check (internal)

B) Unit tests
- Shared config loader tests (env var parsing, precedence, redaction behavior)
- Shared telemetry wrapper tests (required attributes present, no high-cardinality footguns)
- Tool-calling utilities tests (allow-list enforcement, timeout wrapper behavior, schema validation)

C) Dependency + security checks
- Dependabot (or equivalent) enabled.
- Secret scanning:
  - pre-commit hook config checked in
  - CI job fails on detected secrets in commits
- SCA:
  - Python: pip-audit (or equivalent)
  - Node: npm audit (bounded, with allowlist only by Security)
- SBOM generation on releases (nice-to-have; if not now, track as follow-up)

D) Build checks
- Docker build for each template (at minimum) to prevent drift:
  - linux/amd64
  - Ensure images are buildable with pinned deps
- docker-compose validation (where provided)
- Kubernetes manifest basic validation (kubeconform / kubectl --dry-run=client where possible)

E) Docs drift prevention
- Enforce that docs code snippets are sourced from repo files where possible.
- CI job: “snippet extraction” step must succeed; failures block merge.
- Validate env var reference table matches actual config keys (simple script parsing config schema).

E2E smoke tests (staging)
Purpose
- Confirm templates run end-to-end against Redwood staging Hosted API and emit required telemetry.

When it runs
- On merge to main for template directories + shared libs
- Nightly scheduled run for early detection of staging drift
- On release candidate tag (vX.Y.Z-rc.N) before final release

What it tests (minimum)
1) RAG template
- Ingest a small, deterministic corpus (fixtures checked into repo)
- Run a query and assert:
  - Response contains an expected substring (keep this loose to avoid flakiness)
  - Retrieval returned at least 1 chunk
  - Latency under a generous bound (to catch obvious timeouts/regressions)
- Telemetry assertions:
  - Trace exists with required attributes: request_id, template_name, model, route, tenant (test tenant), error_class if error
  - Metrics emitted: request_count, request_latency_ms, token_usage (input/output) (names per contract)
  - Logs include correlation fields (request_id/trace_id) and do not include API key

2) Agents template
- Run a deterministic tool call flow using stub tools (no network) and ensure:
  - Tool allow-list prevents unapproved tool name
  - Tool timeout wrapper triggers clean error (not a hang)
  - Tool output schema validation fails with clear message for invalid payload
- Streaming path:
  - Start streaming response and verify reconnection/backoff logic does not spam retries

3) Combined RAG+agent
- Retrieval exposed as a tool; run a “planner -> retrieve -> answer” flow
- Confirm prompt injection guardrails are in place (basic negative test: injected instruction to call unknown tool should be blocked)

Stability / flake management
- Known failure modes:
  - Staging capacity variability affecting latency
  - External dependencies (vector DB container pulls)
  - Network blips (esp. streaming)
- Mitigations:
  - Generous timeouts with explicit caps; prefer ‘fail fast with helpful logs’
  - Retries with jitter for transient network errors only
  - Record per-run artifacts:
    - test logs (structured)
    - trace IDs and deep links to Console if available
    - snapshot of config (with secrets redacted)
- Flake policy:
  - If a job flakes twice in 24h, it becomes ‘required but quarantine-able’ only with SRE approval and a follow-up ticket created.
  - Quarantine must include expiry date and owner.

Release checklist (human steps)
Pre-release (RC)
- [ ] All required CI jobs green on main
- [ ] E2E smoke tests green within last 24h
- [ ] Dependency scans clean (or documented exceptions)
- [ ] Release notes draft generated and reviewed
- [ ] Compatibility matrix updated
- [ ] Docs snippet sync job green (no drift)
- [ ] Observability pack changes aligned with telemetry contract

Release
- [ ] Create tag vX.Y.Z (and vX.Y.Z for observability pack if changed)
- [ ] Publish GitHub release with notes
- [ ] Update docs site references to ‘latest’ tag (or template download instructions)
- [ ] Announce in #announcements (internal) + #devex (internal support)

Post-release monitoring (first 48h)
- Monitor quickstart dashboards:
  - Error rate by error_class
  - 429 rate (spikes indicate default retries/backoff issues or too-low quotas)
  - Timeout rate
  - Streaming disconnect rate (where measurable)
- Support readiness:
  - Ensure known issues doc updated with new release info
  - Ensure ‘how to upgrade’ snippet is accurate

Deprecation policy (draft)
Scope
- Applies to template releases, template contract versions (env vars + required behavior), and telemetry contract versions.

Signals a deprecation
- Any of:
  - env var rename/removal
  - endpoint rename/removal in template service API (e.g., /query -> /chat)
  - removal of a supported backend path from default template
  - telemetry metric rename/removal where dashboards depend on it

Deprecation window
- For breaking changes (MAJOR):
  - Minimum 90 days deprecation notice from first announcement to EOL
  - Provide migration guide + mechanical steps
  - Maintain compatibility shim where feasible for at least one minor cycle (example: accept old env var but warn)
- For MINOR-level deprecations (soft):
  - Announce in release notes + docs banner
  - Keep old behavior for at least two minor releases (N and N+1)

Communication channels
- GitHub release notes + changelog
- Docs site banner on the relevant template pages
- ‘Upgrade/migration’ section in README
- Internal: #support and #devex heads-up for ticket triage

Support + maintenance policy
- Supported: latest 2 minor releases of templates (bug fixes, doc fixes)
- Security-only: previous minor release for 30 days after it leaves supported window
- EOL: no fixes; docs site should point to the latest supported release

Open questions / TODO
- Do we want a single combined release for redwood-quickstarts + observability-pack (same tag), or keep them independent but linked?
- Should we publish template artifacts (zip/tar) attached to releases for easier consumption in locked-down environments?
- Confirm the exact telemetry contract version naming (e.g., quickstart-telemetry-contract v1) and how it’s referenced in code.
- Decide whether k8s manifest validation is required on every PR or only on merge.
- Decide whether to require a ‘Console deep link’ emitted in logs for smoke tests (nice-to-have; could increase coupling).

Notes to self (from early feedback)
- SRE ask: default alerts must be non-noisy; CI should include a ‘no high-cardinality labels’ check for metrics.
- SDK ask: streaming retry logic needs to be consistent across templates; avoid every template re-implementing backoff.
- Docs ask: snippet extraction failures are blocking; keep this job fast and with actionable errors.
